answer: At every inlet, an agent must post a bond linked to a persistent collateral anchor before it can trade or vote. The protocol grants influence only in proportion to locked value, rather than to the number of account names, and burns the bond when a challenge proves coordinated double-registration. A Sybil attacker therefore must buy and lock separate scarce capital for every fake identity, risking a direct loss; a saffron trader gains more by staying honest.
